newsitem.title: CHINA: China urged to rein in inflation over long term.
newsitem.headline: China urged to rein in inflation over long term.

text.p: China should extend its battle against inflation well into the next century to maintain healthy economic growth, the China Business Times said on Thursday.
"People should not lower their vigilance against inflation," the newspaper said, quoting economist Wang Yongzhi of the State Planning Commission.
"Inflation pressure will still exist in the 1996-2000 period and well into the first 10 years of the next century," he was quoted as saying.
The government should maintain its anti-inflation policies, including tight financial and monetary policies in the next decades, he said.
China has kept a tight lid on credit since 1993 to try to cool runaway inflation, although recently it has boosted bank loans to selected state firms and key industries as inflation has eased.
China's economic growth was expected to reach about 9.0 percent in the 1996-2000 period before falling to about 8.0 percent in 2001-2010 and declining to 7.0 percent in 2011-2020, he said.
Economic growth in 1996 was 10.2 percent and China has set a target of 8.0 percent growth for this year.
Inflation up to the turn of the century was projected at 7.0-8.0 percent, the official said.
In the first 10 years of the 21st century, inflation was expected to hold at 6.0-7.0 percent and to range between 4.0-6.0 percent in 2011-2020, he said.
China has set a target of benchmark retail price inflation of 6.0 percent for 1997, compared with 6.1 percent in 1996. Inflation in 1995 was 14.8 percent.
